docs.text: Driver ADS9324 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the TI ADS9324, a 16-channel, 16-bit, 1 MSPS simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC with an integrated programmable-gain front end and an SPI interface. It starts the chip safely, programs every channel, reads and decodes a whole frame of 16 samples, and runs the window comparator and the calibration, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves SPI frames and waits; it does the rest: the reset sequence, the identity check, the three register banks (the AIN9 to AIN16 bank is laid out in reverse order, and the driver knows), the data frame in every lane and word format, unit conversion and bounded waits. 16-channel simultaneous-sampling ADC ADS9324 Texas Instruments Function 16 channels sampled together, 16 bits each, up to 1 MSPS per channel; differential or single-ended inputs Inputs 1 MΩ input impedance; ±2.5 V, ±5 V, ±6.25 V, ±10 V and ±12.5 V ranges per channel; 25 kHz or 325 kHz bandwidth Interface SPI for the registers (24-bit frames, up to 60 MHz); data on 1, 2, 4 or 8 lanes, 16 or 24 bits per channel Digital Block, moving-average and FIR filters; offset, gain and phase calibration; window comparator; alarm pin Reference Internal 4.096 V or external on REFIO Supply 5 V analog, 1.8 V analog, 1.7 V to 3.6 V I/O What you get ¶ One object per chip. ADS9324<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , Timeout , DeviceIdMismatch or UnexpectedReset . See API guide . A configuration that is checked. Config{} is the datasheet's initialisation example; Validate() rejects an impossible combination before any bus traffic, and CheckedConfig rejects it at compile time. See Configuration . Per-channel settings that land on the right channel. The AIN9 to AIN16 registers are in reverse order; the driver maps every channel and the host tests prove it for all 16. See Architecture . Every data format. 1, 2, 4 or 8 lanes, 16- or 24-bit words, the diagnostic byte and the randomizer, all 15 channel modes. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks and a delay, plus optional CONVST, RESET, DRDY and lane-capture hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no floating point. See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against an independent model of the chip. See Testing and CI . Datasheet ¶ Document Revision Get it Datasheet: ADS9324 16-Channel, 16-Bit, 1MSPS, Simultaneous-Sampling SAR ADC With Integrated Analog Front-End (Texas Instruments SBASB22) -, 2025-12 PDF · vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, read the 16 channels. Hardware Pins, supplies, reference, bus settings and timing. Contract What the driver promises, what it needs, threading and errors. API guide Initialise, configure, measure, set windows and calibrate, task by task. Porting Implement the port for your MCU. Limitations What is not supported, and what is not verified on hardware.

docs.text:
API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: initialise, measure, set a range, watch a window, calibrate, handle errors and go to standby. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: ADC transfer function and output codes: 7.3.5 ADC Transfer Function, p. 27 ADC gain and offset error calibration: 7.3.10 ADC Gain and Offset Error Calibration, p. 32 Digital filters and the system phase calibration: 7.3.11 Digital Filter; 7.3.11.1 System Phase Calibration, p. 34 Digital window comparator: 7.3.12 Digital Window Comparator, p. 39 Alarm modes and the DRDY/ALARM pin: 7.3.13 Alarm Modes, Table 7-10, p. 41 Test patterns: 7.3.14.5 Test Patterns for Data Interface, Table 7-14, p. 47 Normal operation and standby: 7.4.2 Normal Operation; 7.4.3 Standby Mode, p. 49 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() , Reset() , Identify() Configuration ApplyConfig() , GetConfig() , SetInput() , SetInterface() , SetFilter() , SetChannels() , SetAlarm() , SetReference() , SetTestPattern() Measurement Convert() , WaitDataReady() , ReadFrame() , MeasureOnce() , ReadAlarmPin() Window comparator ReadWindowFlags() , ClearWindowFlags() Calibration RunAdcCalibration() , DisableAdcCalibration() , IsCalibrationBusy() Power PowerDown() , Wake() , IsPoweredDown() Diagnostics ReadRegister() , GetShadow() , RunDataPathSelfTest() Pure helpers Validate() , RangeMillivolts() , CodeToMicrovolts() , OutputRateHz() , ads9324::GetDriverVersion() Every call that touches the chip returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. Channels are counted from 0: channel 0 is AIN1 and channel 15 is AIN16. Initialise ¶ ads9324 :: Error BringUp ( Adc & adc ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok // with no I/O. After a failure the next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = adc . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "ADS9324 init: %s 
 " , ads9324 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } The constructor stores the port and the configuration ( Config{} unless you pass one) and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the chip. Its first call brings the bus up, waits the power-up time, resets the chip (RESET when Config::hardware_reset is set, otherwise SW_RST), checks DEVICE_ID, clears the reset flag and writes the configuration. Once it has succeeded, EnsureInitialized() returns Ok at once with no I/O, so a caller (or a handler that owns the driver) can call it before every use. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning. No other call starts the chip: before EnsureInitialized() succeeds every read and write returns NotInitialized and sends nothing. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration for the first EnsureInitialized() . Measure ¶ ads9324 :: Result < int32_t > MeasureAin5 ( Adc & adc ) { // CONVST pulse, wait for the result, read and decode one frame (needs // GpioSet() for CONVST). const auto frame = adc . MeasureOnce (); if ( ! frame ) { return ads9324 :: Result < int32_t >:: Failure ( frame . error ); } return ads9324 :: Result < int32_t >:: Success ( frame . value . microvolts [ 4 ]); // AIN5, in microvolts } MeasureOnce() is Convert() , WaitDataReady() and ReadFrame() in one call. Convert() pulses CONVST (high, then low, then high again: the falling edge samples all 16 channels together, and the line is high when the result arrives). MeasureOnce() repeats the pulse as often as one result needs ( PulsesPerResult() ). WaitDataReady() waits for the DRDY pin when Sampling::ready is ReadySource::Pin and the port has GpioGet() , otherwise the conversion time. ReadFrame() clocks the frame out and decodes it into a Frame : Frame field Meaning codes[n] The signed 16-bit code of channel n (0 for a channel that is not in the frame) microvolts[n] The input voltage of channel n, from the code and the channel's range, in integer microvolts raw[n] , low_byte[n] The wire value after derandomizing, and the extra byte of a 24-bit word present_mask , clipped_mask Bit n: channel n is in the frame, or sits at a code limit diag , window_alert , reset_detected The DIAG byte, when Interface::append_diag or randomize adds it Drive CONVST yourself ¶ A port without GpioSet() for CONVST, or a design where a timer or a PWM channel clocks CONVST, calls ReadFrame() after each conversion instead of MeasureOnce() ; the driver then never touches CONVST, except that RunAdcCalibration() and a filter change need pulses and return Unsupported without the hook. Set Sampling::convst_hz to the rate your timer runs, so the timed waits and the output-rate helpers match. With a block-average filter on the external clock, or a FIR filter, one Convert() is one CONVST pulse, but the chip produces a result only after the block ( PulsesPerResult(Filter) pulses); pulse CONVST that many times (a free-running timer does this) before ReadFrame() . MeasureOnce() does it for you. Limitations lists this. Set a range ¶ ads9324 :: Error UseTenVoltRange ( Adc & adc ) { ads9324 :: Input in = adc . GetConfig (). inputs [ 8 ]; // AIN9: the register layout is mirrored, the driver knows in . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: V10 ; // +-10 V full scale in . bandwidth = ads9324 :: Bandwidth :: Wide ; // 280 kHz to 350 kHz low-pass return adc . SetInput ( 8 , in ). error ; // only the registers that change are written } SetInput() takes a channel and an Input : range (±2.5 V, ±5 V, ±6.25 V, ±10 V, ±12.5 V), type (differential, single-ended, single-ended open-wire safe), bandwidth, common-mode correction, offset, gain, phase delay and the window. The registers of the AIN9 to AIN16 bank are in reverse order; SetInput(8, ...) writes AIN9's registers. A call writes only what changed and stores the input only after the chip accepted it. The offset and gain correction helpers OffsetCorrectionFor() and GainCorrectionFor() turn a measured error into the register values. Watch a window ¶ ads9324 :: Error WatchAin3 ( Adc & adc ) { ads9324 :: Input in = adc . GetConfig (). inputs [ 2 ]; in . window = ads9324 :: Window { true , 40 , -40 , 2 }; // alert outside -40..+40 on the top byte, hysteresis 2 if ( auto r = adc . SetInput ( 2 , in ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } ads9324 :: Alarm alarm = adc . GetConfig (). alarm ; alarm . function = ads9324 :: AlarmFunction :: WindowAlert ; // DRDY/ALARM now shows // the window alert return adc . SetAlarm ( alarm ). error ; } ads9324 :: Error AcknowledgeAlerts ( Adc & adc ) { const auto flags = adc . ReadWindowFlags (); // which channels went high (bit n = // AIN n+1) or low if ( ! flags ) { return flags . error ; } std :: printf ( "high 0x%04X low 0x%04X 
 " , static_cast < unsigned > ( flags . value . high ), static_cast < unsigned > ( flags . value . low )); const auto a = adc . ClearWindowFlags ( 0 ); // AIN1 to AIN8 return a ? adc . ClearWindowFlags ( 1 ). error : a . error ; // AIN9 to AIN16 } The window comparator compares the top byte of each code with a high and a low threshold, with hysteresis. The driver writes the thresholds before it enables the window, so no false alert appears between the two writes. With AlarmFunction::WindowAlert the DRDY/ALARM pin shows the alert ( ReadAlarmPin() reads it, with active_low applied); the flags per channel are latched until ClearWindowFlags() clears a group. Alarm::pulse makes the pin a pulse instead of a level (window alert only); AlarmFunction::OrMasked needs or_mask_acknowledged , because the sense of the source mask is not verified ( Limitations ). Choose a filter ¶ ads9324 :: Error AverageSixteen ( Adc & adc ) { ads9324 :: Filter f {}; f . kind = ads9324 :: FilterKind :: MovingAverage ; f . length = ads9324 :: AverageLength :: X16 ; return adc . SetFilter ( f ). error ; // the driver pulses SYSREF after the write, as the chip needs } One digital filter at a time: block average, moving average or a FIR filter (FIR1 to FIR5 and FIR7). The driver pulses SYSREF (CONVST low, high, low) after a filter write, as the chip requires; that needs GpioSet() for CONVST. A filter and the ADC calibration exclude each other: switch the filter off first. Calibrate ¶ ads9324 :: Error Calibrate ( Adc & adc ) { // Needs no digital filter. Single shot: about 125 ms, then the chip keeps the // result. return adc . RunAdcCalibration () . error ; // Refused when a filter is on, Timeout when CALIB_BUSY stays set } RunAdcCalibration() removes the converter's own offset and gain error ( Config::calibration chooses which, and whether CONVST runs single-shot or free). It waits for CALIB_BUSY with a bound of 150 ms. The chip keeps the result as long as ADC_CAL_MODE stays set, so the driver leaves it set; DisableAdcCalibration() removes the correction. Check the data path ¶ RunDataPathSelfTest() writes a different constant test pattern to every channel, reads a frame and compares each channel with its own pattern, then restores the configuration. It proves the data lanes, the word format and the channel-to-register mapping of both banks on your board, and returns DataMismatch when a channel returns another's value. Run it once at bring-up. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( ads9324 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case ads9324 :: Error :: Bus : case ads9324 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check the SPI wiring, the mode and the chip select" ; case ads9324 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset : return "the chip lost its configuration: call EnsureInitialized() again" ; case ads9324 :: Error :: DataMismatch : return "all zeros or all ones on the data line: check SDOUT and the " "supplies" ; case ads9324 :: Error :: Refused : return "the chip is in standby or a filter is on: Wake(), or SetFilter() " "with None first" ; default : return ads9324 :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring; retry, or Reset(Software) , or Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() Error::Timeout A reset, the DRDY pin or a calibration did not finish Check the supplies, the reference and CONVST; raise Sampling::ready_timeout_us Error::DataMismatch The frame is all zeros or all ones Check SDOUT and the supplies; RunDataPathSelfTest() Error::UnexpectedReset The chip reset behind the driver's back EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again Error::VerifyFailed A read-back differs from what was written Lower the clock; check the supplies Error::Refused Standby, or a calibration with a filter on Wake() , or switch the filter off Error::Unsupported A hook the call needs is absent, or the daisy chain was requested Add the hook; the daisy chain is out of scope Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. ads9324::ToString() names an error for a log. Diagnostics ¶ For bring-up and fault finding, the driver keeps what it believes the chip holds and offers one raw access (handbook KB-CPP-119, KB-CPP-129): Call I/O What it gives ReadRegister(bank, address) bank select, command and data frame, no retry The raw 16 bits of one documented register GetLastRegisterReply() none The raw value the last ReadRegister returned GetShadow(bank, address) none The value the driver believes the chip holds Verify::ReadBack (a trailing argument of every setter) one two-frame read per register written VerifyFailed when a register differs Standby ¶ void Standby ( Adc & adc ) { if ( auto r = adc . PowerDown (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "ADS9324 standby failed: %s 
 " , ads9324 :: ToString ( r . error )); return ; } // ... later ... const auto w = adc . Wake (); // waits 30 ms and checks that the registers survived if ( w . error == ads9324 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset ) { ( void ) adc . EnsureInitialized (); // they did not: start again } } PowerDown() writes the standby bit; until Wake() every other call returns Refused . Wake() waits 30 ms and checks that the chip kept its registers (GEN_CFG3 against the shadow and the reset flag). Deinitialize() is the standby write plus NotInitialized afterwards: Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() is also the recovery after a fault. Next: Configuration .

docs.text: void Standby ( Adc & adc ) { if ( auto r = adc . PowerDown (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "ADS9324 standby failed: %s \n " , ads9324 :: ToString ( r . error )); return ; } // ... later ... const auto w = adc . Wake (); // waits 30 ms and checks that the registers survived if ( w . error == ads9324 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset ) { ( void ) adc . EnsureInitialized (); // they did not: start again } } PowerDown() writes the standby bit; until Wake() every other call returns Refused . Wake() waits 30 ms and checks that the chip kept its registers (GEN_CFG3 against the shadow and the reset flag). Deinitialize() is the standby write plus NotInitialized afterwards: Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() is also the recovery after a fault. Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when you read a frame. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Data interface: lanes, word length and channel modes: 7.3.14 Data Interface; 7.3.14.1 ADC Channel Modes, Table 7-12, p. 42 Register write and read frames: 7.5 Programming; 7.5.1 Register Write Operation; 7.5.2 Register Read Operation, p. 50 Initialization example, single lane on SDOUT: 7.5.3 Initialization Example - Single Lane Mode on SDOUT, p. 51 Common registers: 8.1 ADS93xx Common Registers, p. 53 Channel registers AIN1 to AIN8: 8.2 AIN1 - AIN8 Channel Registers, p. 64 Channel registers AIN9 to AIN16 (reversed order): 8.3 AIN9 - AIN16 Channel Registers, p. 86 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp public calls ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/ads9324.hpp , src/ads9324.ipp Lifecycle, setters, conversions, calibration, standby, errors Types and encoding inc/ads9324_types.hpp , inc/ads9324_encode.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config and Validate() ; the pure, constexpr Encode() of a Config into registers; the frame decoder Registers inc/ads9324_registers.hpp The three banks, 116 registers, fields, reset values, the channel-to-register mapping Port contract inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin and GpioSignal , the SpiPort concept, the 24-bit register framing Platform port Your class Bus bring-up and frame transfers, optionally delays, the CONVST, RESET and DRDY pins, lane capture and logging Kconfig layer inc/ads9324_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig The three register banks ¶ The chip has a common bank (18 registers) and one bank per group of eight channels (49 registers each), selected by BANK_SEL. The AIN9 to AIN16 bank is laid out in reverse order : bank-local index 15 - channel , so AIN16 is local index 0 (the low byte of the first two-channel register), where the AIN1 to AIN8 bank puts AIN1 first. The driver keeps one function, reg::Locate(channel) , that returns the bank and the local index; every register layout rule (the low half of a two-channel register belongs to the even local index) is written once on local indexes. A host test programs every channel with a distinct value and checks the model's registers channel by channel, and the data-path self-test proves the same on the data side. Writing the configuration ¶ detail::Encode(Config) is a pure function from a Config to a RegisterImage : the register values plus a mask of the registers it touches. ApplyConfig() and every setter encode the new configuration, compare it with the shadow (the register values the driver believes the chip holds) and write only what differs, in this order: the window thresholds before DWC_EN, the filter registers, and a SYSREF pulse (CONVST 0, 1, 0) after the filter write, as the datasheet requires. The shadow is updated after each accepted write, and the stored Config only when the whole call succeeded. With Verify::ReadBack each written register is read back and compared. One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as ADS9324<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: MeasureOnce() Core->>Port: GpioSet(Convst, ACTIVE) Core->>Port: GpioSet(Convst, INACTIVE) Note over Core: the falling edge samples all 16 channels Core->>Port: GpioGet(DrdyAlarm) or DelayUs(1.25 us) Core->>Port: Transfer(zeros, rx, N bytes) Port-->>Core: true, N bytes Note over Core: derandomize, DIAG, codes to microvolts Core-->>App: Result<Frame> Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by named concepts. GpioSet , GpioGet , CaptureLanes , DelayUs and Log are detected with Declares* and Has* concepts in ads9324::detail . A hook that is declared with a wrong signature is a compile error, never a silent fallback; a hook that is absent falls back in a documented way. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no floating point. The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state; voltages are integer microvolts. A configuration is data. Validate() and Encode() are constexpr, so a fixed board configuration can be proved valid, and its register image checked, at compile time ( CheckedConfig ). The daisy chain is a seam, not a feature. DaisyChain is in Config so the layout is stable, and Validate() refuses it; see Limitations . docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every field of ads9324::Config , how a configuration is checked, the data interface, and the optional Kconfig layer. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Supplies, reference and input ranges: 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p. 6 Analog inputs and the input clamps: 7.3.1 Analog Inputs; 7.3.2 Input Clamp Protection Circuit, p. 25 PGA, input ranges, common-mode range and bandwidth: 7.3.4 Programmable Gain Amplifier (PGA), Tables 7-1 and 7-2, p. 26 ADC transfer function and output codes: 7.3.5 ADC Transfer Function, p. 27 Reference selection: 7.3.6 Reference, Table 7-3, p. 28 Open-wire safe mode: 7.3.7 Open Wire Safe Mode, p. 30 System offset and gain calibration: 7.3.8 System Offset Calibration; 7.3.9 System Gain Calibration, p. 31 Digital filters and the system phase calibration: 7.3.11 Digital Filter; 7.3.11.1 System Phase Calibration, p. 34 Block average, moving average and FIR filters: 7.3.11.2 to 7.3.11.4, p. 35 Digital window comparator: 7.3.12 Digital Window Comparator, p. 39 Alarm modes and the DRDY/ALARM pin: 7.3.13 Alarm Modes, Table 7-10, p. 41 Data interface: lanes, word length and channel modes: 7.3.14 Data Interface; 7.3.14.1 ADC Channel Modes, Table 7-12, p. 42 Diagnostic byte and the randomizer: 7.3.14.3 Diagnostic Flags; 7.3.14.4 ADC Output Data Randomizer, p. 44 Output drive strength and output delay: 7.3.14.6 Digital Output Drive Strength Control; 7.3.14.7 Digital Output Delay Adjustment, p. 48 Common registers: 8.1 ADS93xx Common Registers, p. 53 Channel registers AIN1 to AIN8: 8.2 AIN1 - AIN8 Channel Registers, p. 64 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Fields ¶ Config{} is the datasheet's initialisation example (Table 7-18) laid over the reset values of every other register: it reads all 16 channels as 16-bit words in one lane on SDOUT, with the ±5 V differential range on every channel. ChipResetConfig() is the chip's own reset state (eight lanes on D7 to D0) for code that needs it. Fields with a unit carry it in the name; voltages are integer microvolts. Field Default Range Registers interface One lane on SDOUT, 16-bit, two's complement Data interface GEN_CFG3, XOR_BITS_CTL, GEN_CFG4, DIG_DELAY_CFG reference Pin Pin , Internal , External ANA_CFG1 inputs[16] Differential, ±5 V, low bandwidth, no correction, window off Per channel Both channel banks filter None Filters DIG_FILTER, GEN_CFG5 channels All 16 16, 8 (2 groups), 4 (4 groups), 2 (8 groups) ANA_CFG2 low_speed_crosstalk false CH_XTALK_LOW_SPEED; for under 100 kSPS per channel alarm DRDY, active high, level Alarm DRDY_ALARM_SEL, GEN_CFG4 sampling.convst_hz 100,000 100,000 to 1,000,000 driver only: the timed waits sampling.ready Time Time , Pin driver only sampling.ready_timeout_us 10,000 1 to 200,000 driver only sampling.reject_stuck_frames true driver only: all-0x00 or all-0xFF is DataMismatch correction Offset and gain stages on GEN_CFG5 of the channel banks calibration Not at start, offset and gain, single shot ADC_CAL_CTL test_pattern[2] Off One per group of eight channels TP_CFG, TP_AIN window_glitch[2] 0 0 to 15 per group DWC glitch filter daisy Off Validate() refuses enabled Limitations supply 0 (not checked) AVDD_5V 4750 to 5250, AVDD_1V8 1700 to 1900, IOVDD 1700 to 3600 mV driver only hardware_reset false Needs GpioSet() for RESET driver only Start from Config{} and change fields: ads9324 :: Config SixteenChannelTenVolt () { ads9324 :: Config c {}; // Table 7-18: 16 channels, 16 bits, one lane on SDOUT for ( auto & in : c . inputs ) { in . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: V10 ; // every channel +-10 V } c . sampling . convst_hz = 200'000 ; // 100 kHz to 1 MHz; checked by Validate() c . interface . append_diag = true ; // one DIAG byte per frame: reset and window flags return c ; // ads9324::Validate(c) checks it without the chip } ads9324 :: Error StartTenVolt ( MyPort & port ) { static ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port , SixteenChannelTenVolt ()); // stored, no I/O return adc . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // InvalidArgument if the config is out of range } Per channel ¶ Input holds everything the chip stores for one channel: type (differential, single-ended, single-ended open-wire safe), range (±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10 or ±12.5 V), bandwidth (25.5 kHz, or 280 kHz to 350 kHz by range), cm_correction , offset_quarter_lsb (-512 to 511), gain (-8192 to 8191, the result is multiplied by 1 + gain / 65536 ), phase_delay (0 to 255 CONVST periods) and the window ( enabled , high_code , low_code , hysteresis ). The channels of one bank share a type class: a bank cannot mix differential and single-ended inputs ( Validate() returns InvalidArgument ), because the datasheet sets the common-mode range per bank. Data interface ¶ Interface chooses how a conversion leaves the chip: Field Values Notes lanes One , Two , Four , Eight Lanes other than One cannot use SDOUT: the data is on D7 to D0 and needs CaptureLanes() data_on_sdout true One lane on SDOUT ( true ) or on D7 ( false ) length Bits16 , Bits24 24 bits adds an extra byte per channel format TwosComplement , OffsetBinary Offset binary cannot be combined with a window append_diag false One DIAG byte at the end of the frame: window alert and reset flags randomize false XORs the data with a PRBS and appends the PRBS byte; needs 16-bit words drive Normal 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x or 2x output drive delay_ns[9] 0 Output delay 0 to 5 ns for SDOUT and D0 to D7 ChannelSelect picks the channels in the frame: all 16, or a group of 8, 4 or 2 (Table 7-12). FrameBytes() says how long the frame is, FrameChannels() which channels it carries, and detail::DecodeFrame() is the pure function that turns bytes into codes (host-testable on its own). Filters ¶ One filter at a time ( FilterKind ): BlockAverage and MovingAverage with a length of 2 to 128, or Fir with FIR1 to FIR5 or FIR7 (FIR6 is reserved and absent). A block average can use the chip's internal oversampling clock ( internal_clock ); the average types need a length, and internal_clock applies only to the block average. ResultsPerOutput() , FirDecimation() and OutputRateHz() compute the output rate from the filter and convst_hz . Alarm ¶ Alarm::function is what DRDY/ALARM shows: Drdy , WindowAlert , CalDone , or OrMasked (the OR of sources , needs or_mask_acknowledged ). active_low inverts the pin (for every function), pulse makes the window alert a pulse, and disabled gates the pin off (refused while the ready source is the pin). Validation ¶ ads9324::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() , ApplyConfig() and every setter call it before any I/O. It returns Error::InvalidArgument when an enum holds a value that is not an enumerator, a field is out of its range, or the combination is impossible: lanes other than One with SDOUT, the randomizer with 24-bit words, a bank that mixes differential and single-ended inputs, an average filter with no length, a pulse alarm for anything but the window alert, an OrMasked mask that is empty or not acknowledged, a window with offset binary, a calibration at start with a filter on, or a channel count with a group number outside its range. A requested daisy chain returns Error::Unsupported . A configuration known at build time can be proved valid at build time: // A configuration known at compile time can be proved valid at compile time: // CheckedConfig is consteval and refuses to compile an invalid one. constexpr ads9324 :: CheckedConfig kFixed { ads9324 :: Config {}}; ads9324 :: Error StartFixed ( MyPort & port ) { static ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port , kFixed . Get ()); return adc . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } An invalid CheckedConfig does not compile; a compile-fail test checks that. Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows ADS9324 16-channel ADC when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options reach the code only through inc/ads9324_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: ads9324 :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port , ads9324 :: KconfigDefaults ()); return adc . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Option Default Config field CONFIG_ADS9324_CONVST_HZ 100000 sampling.convst_hz CONFIG_ADS9324_WORD_24_BIT n interface.length CONFIG_ADS9324_APPEND_DIAG n interface.append_diag CONFIG_ADS9324_READY_ON_PIN n sampling.ready CONFIG_ADS9324_READY_TIMEOUT_US 10000 sampling.ready_timeout_us Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} . Both cases are host tests. Next: Porting .

docs.title: Fields

docs.text: Input holds everything the chip stores for one channel: type (differential, single-ended, single-ended open-wire safe), range (±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10 or ±12.5 V), bandwidth (25.5 kHz, or 280 kHz to 350 kHz by range), cm_correction , offset_quarter_lsb (-512 to 511), gain (-8192 to 8191, the result is multiplied by 1 + gain / 65536 ), phase_delay (0 to 255 CONVST periods) and the window ( enabled , high_code , low_code , hysteresis ). The channels of one bank share a type class: a bank cannot mix differential and single-ended inputs ( Validate() returns InvalidArgument ), because the datasheet sets the common-mode range per bank.
docs.title: Per channel

docs.text: Interface chooses how a conversion leaves the chip: Field Values Notes lanes One , Two , Four , Eight Lanes other than One cannot use SDOUT: the data is on D7 to D0 and needs CaptureLanes() data_on_sdout true One lane on SDOUT ( true ) or on D7 ( false ) length Bits16 , Bits24 24 bits adds an extra byte per channel format TwosComplement , OffsetBinary Offset binary cannot be combined with a window append_diag false One DIAG byte at the end of the frame: window alert and reset flags randomize false XORs the data with a PRBS and appends the PRBS byte; needs 16-bit words drive Normal 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x or 2x output drive delay_ns[9] 0 Output delay 0 to 5 ns for SDOUT and D0 to D7 ChannelSelect picks the channels in the frame: all 16, or a group of 8, 4 or 2 (Table 7-12). FrameBytes() says how long the frame is, FrameChannels() which channels it carries, and detail::DecodeFrame() is the pure function that turns bytes into codes (host-testable on its own).
docs.title: Data interface

docs.text: One filter at a time ( FilterKind ): BlockAverage and MovingAverage with a length of 2 to 128, or Fir with FIR1 to FIR5 or FIR7 (FIR6 is reserved and absent). A block average can use the chip's internal oversampling clock ( internal_clock ); the average types need a length, and internal_clock applies only to the block average. ResultsPerOutput() , FirDecimation() and OutputRateHz() compute the output rate from the filter and convst_hz .
docs.title: Filters

docs.text: Alarm::function is what DRDY/ALARM shows: Drdy , WindowAlert , CalDone , or OrMasked (the OR of sources , needs or_mask_acknowledged ). active_low inverts the pin (for every function), pulse makes the window alert a pulse, and disabled gates the pin off (refused while the ready source is the pin).
docs.title: Alarm

docs.text: ads9324::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() , ApplyConfig() and every setter call it before any I/O. It returns Error::InvalidArgument when an enum holds a value that is not an enumerator, a field is out of its range, or the combination is impossible: lanes other than One with SDOUT, the randomizer with 24-bit words, a bank that mixes differential and single-ended inputs, an average filter with no length, a pulse alarm for anything but the window alert, an OrMasked mask that is empty or not acknowledged, a window with offset binary, a calibration at start with a filter on, or a channel count with a group number outside its range. A requested daisy chain returns Error::Unsupported . A configuration known at build time can be proved valid at build time: // A configuration known at compile time can be proved valid at compile time: // CheckedConfig is consteval and refuses to compile an invalid one. constexpr ads9324 :: CheckedConfig kFixed { ads9324 :: Config {}}; ads9324 :: Error StartFixed ( MyPort & port ) { static ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port , kFixed . Get ()); return adc . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } An invalid CheckedConfig does not compile; a compile-fail test checks that.

EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Option Default Config field CONFIG_ADS9324_CONVST_HZ 100000 sampling.convst_hz CONFIG_ADS9324_WORD_24_BIT n interface.length CONFIG_ADS9324_APPEND_DIAG n interface.append_diag CONFIG_ADS9324_READY_ON_PIN n sampling.ready CONFIG_ADS9324_READY_TIMEOUT_US 10000 sampling.ready_timeout_us Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} . docs.text: Contract ¶ What the ADS9324 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Electrical characteristics, power-up and reset times: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics, p. 7 Timing diagrams, DRDY and the data frame: 5.8 Timing Diagrams, p. 12 ADC gain and offset error calibration: 7.3.10 ADC Gain and Offset Error Calibration, p. 32 Diagnostic byte and the randomizer: 7.3.14.3 Diagnostic Flags; 7.3.14.4 ADC Output Data Randomizer, p. 44 Normal operation and standby: 7.4.2 Normal Operation; 7.4.3 Standby Mode, p. 49 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument or Unsupported , nothing sent), brings the bus up, waits the power-up time, resets the chip (RESET when Config::hardware_reset is set, otherwise SW_RST), checks DEVICE_ID and BANK_SEL, waits for the calibration flag to clear and only then writes the configuration. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds. No call initialises or resets the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. A setter changes the stored configuration only after the chip accepted every write; after a failure the driver keeps the old configuration. The driver's shadow of the registers equals the chip after every setter that returns Ok . A setter writes only the registers that change, in the order the chip needs: the window thresholds before the window is enabled, and a SYSREF pulse after a filter change. Every wait is bounded: the power-up and reset waits are constants, the DRDY wait by Sampling::ready_timeout_us , the ADC calibration by 125 ms plus 25 ms. A frame that cannot be a conversion (all bytes 0x00 or all 0xFF , which is what a stuck or floating SDOUT reads) is DataMismatch , not data. Sampling::reject_stuck_frames turns this off for a test pattern. A DIAG byte that reports a reset makes the driver uninitialised and returns UnexpectedReset : the configuration is gone, and the next EnsureInitialized() writes it again. The DIAG byte is off in Config{} , so every configuration call ( ApplyConfig() and the setters, ClearWindowFlags() , ReadWindowFlags() , the calibration calls, RunDataPathSelfTest() , PowerDown() ) first re-sends BANK_SEL, reads DEVICE_ID and DIAG_CTRL, and returns UnexpectedReset with nothing else written when RESET_DETECT_FLAG is set. A reset between two frames that no such call has looked at is seen only by the next data frame with the DIAG byte, the next configuration call or Wake() . A register reply is data only when its last byte (SDOUT[7:0]) is 0x00 ; any other tail is Bus . A stuck-low line reads as zeros and passes that check, so every status read that would accept "idle" or "no reset" ( IsCalibrationBusy() , the end of a calibration wait, Wake() , the reset probe) also reads DEVICE_ID and returns Bus when it is not 0x0004 . After a configuration call fails part-way the layout registers (lanes, word length, channel selection) are unknown: ReadFrame() and MeasureOnce() return Refused until a configuration call succeeds. MeasureOnce() sends as many CONVST pulses as one result needs ( PulsesPerResult() : the FIR decimation, or the block-average length with the external clock) and waits ConversionTimeUs() , the datasheet's (N - 1) x tCYC + 1.25 us . Convert() leaves CONVST high, as Figure 5-7 requires for the internal oversampling clock. Config{} is the datasheet's initialisation example (Table 7-18), which reads all 16 channels as 16-bit words on SDOUT; ChipResetConfig() is the chip's own reset state (eight lanes on D7 to D0). A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() gives Error::Unsupported from the calls that need CONVST or RESET; a missing GpioGet() makes the timed wait the only ready source; a missing Log() logs nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() puts the chip in standby, its lowest-current state, even if that write failed. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates ads9324_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay; optionally CONVST, RESET and DRDY, each at its idle level before the first transfer; lane capture for 2, 4 or 8 lanes; and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ ads9324::Error inside ads9324::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; chip-specific values start at 16. Every value is returned by some call, except the three the chip cannot produce, which a test asserts are never returned. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran since InvalidArgument 2 A Config field or argument is out of range ( Validate() ); nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The calibration flag, the DRDY pin or a reset did not finish in time DeviceIdMismatch 5 DEVICE_ID is not 0x0004 after a reset Crc 6 Never returned: the chip has no CRC on this interface Busy 7 Never returned: the chip has no busy reply DeviceFault 8 Never returned: the chip has no fault flag; kept for the shared set Unsupported 9 A port hook the call needs is absent, or the daisy chain was requested UnexpectedReset 16 The DIAG byte or RESET_DETECT_FLAG reports a reset: the chip lost its configuration. The driver is uninitialised afterwards VerifyFailed 17 A read-back ( Verify::ReadBack ) or the register check after standby differs from what was written Refused 18 The call is not allowed in this state (standby, or a calibration with a digital filter on); nothing was sent DataMismatch 19 A frame is all zeros or all ones, or the data-path self-test read another channel's value The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf , no floating point and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config (340 bytes) and a shadow of the 116 registers: 792 bytes in all. The largest stack buffers are two arrays of 50 bytes (the longest data frame). Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.
docs.title: Contract

docs.title: Coverage matrix

docs.text: One row for each parameter, register field, mode, pin and timing the data sheet specifies. The API column names the symbol of this driver that covers the row. tools/check_matrix.py (part of tools/preflight.sh ) fails when a symbol cited here is not in inc/ , src/ or docs/hardware.yml (a symbol that appears only in a comment does not count), when a test id does not start the name of a TEST_CASE in tests/ , when a row is malformed, or when the counts below are wrong. The Test column names a topic: every test case whose name starts with that id belongs to it, so the table shows where a row is tested, not which assertion proves it. A row the driver does not cover has the status GAP and says so in the API column. Status: OK covered and tested, GUARD the driver restricts the values to the documented ones, TODO the data sheet leaves it open or the feature is out of scope for this version, INFO a fact with no driver behaviour, GAP the data sheet value has no symbol in the driver. Total rows 873: OK 675, GUARD 82, TODO 10, INFO 80, GAP 26.

docs.text: Datasheet map ¶ The driver follows the ADS9324 datasheet. This page says which revision, where to get it, and where each part of the driver is described in it, so you can check any behaviour against the source. Section names and page numbers are the datasheet's own (the printed page numbers). docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated ADS9324, through the host port host_ads9324_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/ads9324_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest ads9324_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1 with an ADS9324 on its SPI bus; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_ads9324_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. The apps ¶ App What it shows Source CI ads9324_basic_example Initialise the ADS9324 from menuconfig values and log four of the 16 channels twice a second ads9324_basic_example.cpp yes Build and flash one (from examples/esp32 , ESP-IDF environment loaded): ./scripts/build_app.sh ads9324_basic_example Release ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor ads9324_basic_example Release Source of this table: examples/esp32/app_config.yml . Set up once ¶ git submodule update --init examples/esp32/scripts # the ESP-IDF build scripts cd examples/esp32 . $IDF_PATH /export.sh # ESP-IDF v5.5 ./scripts/build_app.sh list # every app and build type The scripts read app_config.yml (the same file this page's table comes from) and build each app as its own firmware image. docs.text: Hardware ¶ The ADS9324's pins, supplies, reference, bus settings and timing, as the driver uses them. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Features, channel count and the 16 simultaneous samples: 1 Features; 3 Description, p. 1 Pins, package and the data lanes: 4 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 3 Absolute maximum ratings: 5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings, p. 5 Supplies, reference and input ranges: 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p. 6 Electrical characteristics, power-up and reset times: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics, p. 7 SPI and CONVST timing: 5.6 Timing Requirements; 5.7 Switching Characteristics, p. 11 Analog inputs and the input clamps: 7.3.1 Analog Inputs; 7.3.2 Input Clamp Protection Circuit, p. 25 Reference selection: 7.3.6 Reference, Table 7-3, p. 28 Alarm modes and the DRDY/ALARM pin: 7.3.13 Alarm Modes, Table 7-10, p. 41 Reset: 7.4.1 Reset, p. 49 Typical application and input filter: 9.2 Typical Application, Figures 9-1 and 9-2, p. 106 Power-supply decoupling: 9.3 Power Supply Recommendations, Figure 9-4, p. 109 Layout: 9.4 Layout, p. 109 Package outline and ordering: 12 Mechanical, Packaging, and Orderable Information, p. 112 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The ADS9324 is a 16-channel, 16-bit, simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC. Each channel has its own clamp, programmable gain amplifier (1 MΩ input impedance) and ADC; one CONVST edge samples all 16 channels together. The registers are read and written over SPI; the conversion results come out on SDOUT (one lane) or on the D0 to D7 pins (2, 4 or 8 lanes). The driver works with the one package the datasheet lists, the 64-pin VQFN (RSK). Pins ¶ The pinout, the block diagram, the circuit and the two tables on this page are drawn from docs/hardware.yml . Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. The package outline, drawn to scale: ADS9324 package, VQFN-64 Figure description and sources The ADS9324 package seen from the top and, when the height is known, from the side, drawn to scale: 8.0 x 8.0 x 1.0 mm. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side at the stated pitch; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . Inside the chip ¶ Inside the ADS9324 Figure description and sources The ADS9324's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . Typical application ¶ One channel with the internal reference (REFSEL high), the data on SDOUT and the three supplies decoupled as Figure 9-4 shows. The other fifteen channels repeat the input filter of the first. The series resistors and the capacitor of the filter are values you choose: the datasheet gives the matched topology (Figure 9-2) and says to match the source resistance on both inputs, not a value. ADS9324: Typical application Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . docs.text: The ADS9324's pins, supplies, reference, bus settings and timing, as the driver uses them. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Features, channel count and the 16 simultaneous samples: 1 Features; 3 Description, p. 1 Pins, package and the data lanes: 4 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 3 Absolute maximum ratings: 5.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings, p. 5 Supplies, reference and input ranges: 5.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, p. 6 Electrical characteristics, power-up and reset times: 5.5 Electrical Characteristics, p. 7 SPI and CONVST timing: 5.6 Timing Requirements; 5.7 Switching Characteristics, p. 11 Analog inputs and the input clamps: 7.3.1 Analog Inputs; 7.3.2 Input Clamp Protection Circuit, p. 25 Reference selection: 7.3.6 Reference, Table 7-3, p. 28 Alarm modes and the DRDY/ALARM pin: 7.3.13 Alarm Modes, Table 7-10, p. 41 Reset: 7.4.1 Reset, p. 49 Typical application and input filter: 9.2 Typical Application, Figures 9-1 and 9-2, p. 106 Power-supply decoupling: 9.3 Power Supply Recommendations, Figure 9-4, p. 109 Layout: 9.4 Layout, p. 109 Package outline and ordering: 12 Mechanical, Packaging, and Orderable Information, p. 112 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The ADS9324 is a 16-channel, 16-bit, simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC. Each channel has its own clamp, programmable gain amplifier (1 MΩ input impedance) and ADC; one CONVST edge samples all 16 channels together. The registers are read and written over SPI; the conversion results come out on SDOUT (one lane) or on the D0 to D7 pins (2, 4 or 8 lanes). The driver works with the one package the datasheet lists, the 64-pin VQFN (RSK).

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( ads9324_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git external/driver-ads9324 git submodule update --init external/driver-ads9324 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-ads9324 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads9324::ads9324 ) ads9324::ads9324 is an alias of the ads9324 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect ADS9324_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver ADS9324_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-ads9324 -B build-ads9324 cmake --install build-ads9324 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( ads9324 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads9324::ads9324 ) The target is ads9324::ads9324 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated ads9324_version.h go to include/ads9324/inc/ , the template implementation to include/ads9324/src/ads9324.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-ads9324) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-ads9324 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git components/ads9324 ads9324 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml ads9324 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : ads9324 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES ads9324 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. docs.text: Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build.
docs.title: Installation

docs.text: A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( ads9324_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result .
docs.title: Requirements

docs.text: A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git external/driver-ads9324 git submodule update --init external/driver-ads9324 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ).
docs.title: Get the source

docs.text: This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-ads9324 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads9324::ads9324 ) ads9324::ads9324 is an alias of the ads9324 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect ADS9324_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver ADS9324_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI )
docs.title: CMake (any MCU, any host)

docs.text: To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-ads9324 -B build-ads9324 cmake --install build-ads9324 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( ads9324 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads9324::ads9324 ) The target is ads9324::ads9324 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated ads9324_version.h go to include/ads9324/inc/ , the template implementation to include/ads9324/src/ads9324.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ).

docs.text: Limitations ¶ What the driver does not do, what it assumes where the datasheet is silent or contradicts itself, and what is not verified on hardware. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Open-wire safe mode: 7.3.7 Open Wire Safe Mode, p. 30 Block average, moving average and FIR filters: 7.3.11.2 to 7.3.11.4, p. 35 Daisy chain (not supported in v1): 7.3.14.2 Daisy Chain, p. 43 Channel registers AIN9 to AIN16 (reversed order): 8.3 AIN9 - AIN16 Channel Registers, p. 86 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Out of scope: the daisy chain ¶ The datasheet's daisy chain (section 7.3.14.2, Figure 7-29) shares CS and SCLK between several ADS9324 and passes each device's SDOUT to the next one's SDI. The driver leaves it out of version 1 and keeps the seam: Why. In a chain a register read or write takes 32 SCLK per device instead of 24, so a single driver object cannot send one chip's frame; the frame belongs to the whole chain, with the position ( DAISY_CHN_LOC ) and the size ( DAISY_CHN_NUM ) programmed in every device. The chain works only with 1, 2 or 4 data lanes on D0 to D7, never with the data on SDOUT, which is the driver's default path. Doing it right needs a chain-level object and a host model of several chips, and neither exists yet. What happens if you ask. Config::daisy exists, so the layout does not change when the support arrives; Validate() returns Error::Unsupported when daisy.enabled is set, EnsureInitialized() returns it before any I/O, the daisy-chain registers are never written, and CheckedConfig does not compile (a compile-fail test checks it). What to do instead. Use one driver object per chip, each with its own chip select; the chips may share SCLK and SDI. Behaviours to know ¶ Continuous-mode calibration needs a running CONVST. CalibrationTrigger::Continuous waits 100,000 CONVST periods (Table 7-7) and then reads CALIB_BUSY_FLAG; the chip counts the periods only while CONVST toggles, so a timer must drive CONVST during the wait. With no CONVST the calibration starts at the next pulse and the data after it is not valid until it ends. CalibrationTrigger::SingleShot needs no timer. The randomizer's XOR_BITS_CTL code. The register table gives 0x00F1; a note in the datasheet says 0x00C1. The driver writes 0x00F1 and only that value or 0x0000. If a bench read shows a chip that wants the other value, change reg::kXorBitsRandomizer and nothing else. Coverage of the datasheet. Coverage matrix lists every parameter the datasheet specifies with the symbol that covers it; rows marked GAP are values the driver has no symbol for (limits and delays that are documented in Hardware only), and tools/check_matrix.py fails when a cited symbol is missing. Block average, FIR and Convert() . Convert() is one CONVST pulse. With a block-average filter on the external clock, or a FIR filter, the chip delivers a result only after the block: MeasureOnce() pulses CONVST PulsesPerResult(Filter) times; with your own timer, pulse that many times and then call ReadFrame() . Stuck frames are errors. A frame of all 0x00 or all 0xFF is DataMismatch by default ( Sampling::reject_stuck_frames ): it is what a floating SDOUT reads. Turn it off for a test pattern that really produces it. One calibration at a time with a filter off. RunAdcCalibration() refuses to run with a digital filter on. OrMasked alarm. The sense of the ALRM_MASK bits is not verified (A41); the call needs Alarm::or_mask_acknowledged . Only documented codes. The reserved register codes are unreachable: the enumerations hold the documented values only (for example TP_MODE 1 is not offered, A22). Assumptions where the datasheet is silent or contradicts itself ¶ Each row has a knob in the host-test chip model ( tests/mock_ads9324.hpp , Knobs ), so the alternatives are testable. the alternative. A real chip that behaves differently shows up on the bench steps below, not in the host tests. Not verified on hardware ¶ Nothing in this driver is verified on a real ADS9324: the host tests run against a model written from the datasheet. The bench steps: EnsureInitialized() returns Ok (DEVICE_ID 0x0004 ) at your SPI clock; try 1 MHz first. This confirms mode 0 (A1) and the reset time (A3). RunDataPathSelfTest() passes with the inputs unconnected: the data format, the lanes and the mirrored channel mapping. Apply a known voltage to AIN9 and AIN16 and check microvolts on the right channel: the mirrored bank (A19). Run RunAdcCalibration() and check the code of a grounded input: the calibration timing (A36, A39). With 2, 4 or 8 lanes, the packing of your CaptureLanes() against SDOUT mode (the bit order is assumed). The window alert with a pulse alarm and the OrMasked source mask (A41). MISRA C++:2023 CodeQL scanning and the ESP32 builds run in CI only; the repository's local checks run the other gates ( Testing and CI ).

docs.text: Platforms ¶ The driver is MCU-agnostic: inc/ and src/ contain no SDK, RTOS or vendor header. A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_ads9324_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_ads9324_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds. The root CMakeLists.txt also covers ESP-IDF: under ESP_PLATFORM it registers the repository as a component (a repository scaffolded without the ESP32 platform adds that branch back from the template when it needs it). Zephyr modules, Arduino library manifests and PlatformIO manifests are added only when a product needs them, and an example is added only together with a CI job that builds it. Add a platform ¶ The add-port skill has the details per MCU. In short: Create examples/<platform>/ with the port ( <platform>_ads9324_port.hpp ), a small example program and a README with the wiring and the expected output. The folder is self-contained: it carries its own port and builds on its own. Build it in CI: a job in .github/workflows/ that builds the example, needed by the CI gate . A platform that CI does not build is not added. If its build system cannot use the root CMakeLists.txt , add the smallest manifest it needs, and say why in the pull request. Never put platform code in inc/ or src/ . Add a row to the table above and a page section if the platform needs one.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Pins, package and the data lanes: 4 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 3 SPI and CONVST timing: 5.6 Timing Requirements; 5.7 Switching Characteristics, p. 11 Timing diagrams, DRDY and the data frame: 5.8 Timing Diagrams, p. 12 Data interface: lanes, word length and channel modes: 7.3.14 Data Interface; 7.3.14.1 ADC Channel Modes, Table 7-12, p. 42 Output drive strength and output delay: 7.3.14.6 Digital Output Drive Strength Control; 7.3.14.7 Digital Output Delay Adjustment, p. 48 Register write and read frames: 7.5 Programming; 7.5.1 Register Write Operation; 7.5.2 Register Read Operation, p. 50 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from ads9324::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the ads9324::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex frame of len bytes with CS low for all of them. rx is nullptr for writes. false on any bus error void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Drive RESET and CONVST; false if the pin write failed or the pin is not wired bool GpioGet(CtrlPin, bool& high) noexcept no Read DRDY/ALARM; set high to the raw level bool CaptureLanes(uint8_t lanes, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept no Clock a data frame in on 2, 4 or 8 lanes (or 1 lane on D7) void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame, CS held low for all `len` bytes (3 for a register, up to 50 for // the data). `rx` is nullptr for writes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the power-up and reset times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep CS low for all len bytes; the chip decodes the frame when CS rises. A register frame is 3 bytes; a data frame is up to 50 bytes ( kMaxFrameBytes ). Never split a frame into several transfers. Buffers. The driver owns the transmit and receive buffers (members of the driver object, no heap, never on the caller's stack), so a DMA that reads them reaches them; a port that needs DMA-capable memory places the driver object there. The bus requirements below : mode 0, MSB first, up to kMaxSdoutClockHz when the port reads SDOUT ( kMaxClockHz for writes only). Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. A transmit buffer of zeros while reading data. The driver sends zeros during a data frame so that no register is written by accident; do not replace them. Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the ADS9324 needs from the bus as constexpr values in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as the ESP32 example port does, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning (datasheet 5.6) kSpiMode 0 CPOL 0, CPHA 0 (derived from the timing diagram: the datasheet names no mode) kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 60'000'000 f_SCLK max (section 5.6), for writes kMaxSdoutClockHz 29'000'000 f_SCLK max when the port reads SDOUT in mode 0: the 17 ns td_CKDO must fit half a period (A2) kMinCsHighNs 16 CS high between two frames, thi_CS kContinuousWord false SCLK may pause inside a frame; only CS framing matters kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs 16 , 16 CS low to the first SCLK edge, last SCLK edge to CS high kFrameIsAtomic true CS stays low for a whole frame; the chip decodes it when CS rises kFrameBits 24 A register frame: 8 address bits and 16 data bits Control pins ¶ Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output and before the driver's first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018). Configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards gives the chip a pulse it did not ask for, for example a reset or a conversion. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle level Before the first transfer Reset RESET active low high ( INACTIVE ) Set high, then enable the output Convst CONVST the falling edge samples; ACTIVE is high high ( ACTIVE ) Set high, then enable the output: the driver leaves CONVST high after each pulse DrdyAlarm DRDY/ALARM active high, an input Configure as an input GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. A pin tied on the board needs no hook. Convert() is one CONVST pulse: ACTIVE , then INACTIVE (the falling edge samples), then ACTIVE again, so CONVST is high before DRDY rises (Figure 5-7). Optional hooks ¶ The driver finds the optional hooks at compile time with named concepts, in one place ( ads9324::detail ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or the call returns Error::Unsupported ; it never skips a step silently, and a hook declared with the wrong signature does not compile. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() The power-up and reset times, the timed ready wait, calibration polling Compile error (every port needs it) GpioSet() RESET ( Config::hardware_reset , Reset(Hardware) ) and CONVST ( Convert() , MeasureOnce() , the SYSREF pulse after a filter change, single-shot calibration) Unsupported from those calls; drive CONVST yourself and use ReadFrame() GpioGet() The DRDY pin wait ( Sampling::ready = ReadySource::Pin ) and ReadAlarmPin() The timed wait; ReadAlarmPin() returns Unsupported CaptureLanes() A data frame on 2, 4 or 8 lanes ReadFrame() returns Unsupported for those lanes; one lane on SDOUT needs no hook Log() One line per lifecycle event or failure Nothing is logged CaptureLanes(lanes, rx, len) clocks len bytes of the frame and packs the bits most significant first, so that every lane count returns the byte stream the 1-lane SDOUT mode would ( lanes is 1, 2, 4 or 8). With 8 lanes each clock yields one byte with D7 as the most significant bit; with 4 lanes two clocks yield a byte (D7 to D4, the high nibble first); with 2 lanes four clocks (D7 and D6 first). This packing follows the data-interface figures of section 7.3.14 and is not verified on hardware ; the host tests check it only against the chip model. A port with every hook: class FullPort : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits (power-up, reset, conversions, // calibration). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: RESET and CONVST on GPIOs. ACTIVE means "asserted": RESET is // active low on the pin, so ACTIVE is a low level there; CONVST is a high // pulse, so ACTIVE is a high level. bool GpioSet ( ads9324 :: CtrlPin pin , ads9324 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = signal == ads9324 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case ads9324 :: CtrlPin :: Reset : return platform_gpio_write ( kResetGpio , ! active ); case ads9324 :: CtrlPin :: Convst : return platform_gpio_write ( kConvstGpio , active ); default : return false ; } } // Optional: the DRDY/ALARM pin as an input. Report the raw level; the driver // applies the polarity. bool GpioGet ( ads9324 :: CtrlPin pin , bool & high ) noexcept { if ( pin != ads9324 :: CtrlPin :: DrdyAlarm ) { return false ; } high = platform_gpio_read ( kDrdyGpio ); return true ; } // Optional: only for 2, 4 or 8 data lanes. Clock the lanes for `len` bytes of // the frame and pack the bits as the Porting page describes. bool CaptureLanes ( uint8_t lanes , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_lanes_capture ( lanes , rx , len ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never // formats; the port does. void Log ( ads9324 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > ads9324 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kResetGpio = 11 ; static constexpr int kConvstGpio = 4 ; static constexpr int kDrdyGpio = 5 ; }; ads9324 :: Error RecoverWithResetPin ( ads9324 :: ADS9324 < FullPort >& adc ) { // With GpioSet() this pulses RESET and writes the stored configuration again; // a port without it gets Error::Unsupported. return adc . Reset ( ads9324 :: ResetKind :: Hardware ). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void , a GpioGet() that returns void , a CaptureLanes() with a narrowed parameter or a Log() that returns int is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check each rule. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_ads9324_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_ads9324_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook except CaptureLanes() (the data is on one lane). Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that DEVICE_ID read 0x0004 . Call RunDataPathSelfTest() : every channel returns its own test pattern, which proves the data lanes, the word format and the channel-to-register mapping of both banks on your wiring. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.
