docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then read the 16 channels from your MCU: wire the chip, write a small port class, call two driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Pins, package and the data lanes: 4 Pin Configuration and Functions, p. 3 Initialization example, single lane on SDOUT: 7.5.3 Initialization Example - Single Lane Mode on SDOUT, p. 51 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated ADS9324, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/ads9324_host_example ADS9324 driver 0.1.0 on the host ads9324: initialised AIN1 -3996 mV ... AIN16 3503 mV window alert pin asserted, low flags 0x0004 calibration done, mode kept: idle The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU ADS9324 Notes SPI SCLK SCLK Mode 0, up to 60 MHz; 1 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI SDI SPI MISO SDOUT The registers and, in the default configuration, the data of all 16 channels GPIO (chip select) CS Low for the whole frame: one transfer per frame GPIO CONVST Idles high; the falling edge samples all 16 channels. A timer may drive it instead GPIO RESET Idles high; optional, tie it high if the port has no hook GPIO input DRDY/ALARM Optional: with it the driver waits for the result, without it for the conversion time 5 V, 1.8 V, 1.7 V to 3.6 V AVDD_5V, AVDD_1V8, IOVDD 1 µF and 0.1 µF at each supply pin GND GND, REFM, exposed pad REFSEL high selects the internal reference (the default). The Hardware page has the full pin list, the reference and the timing. Every analog input needs a series resistor: the datasheet rating is ±18 V. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the ads9324::ads9324 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git external/driver-ads9324 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves frames. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame, CS held low for all `len` bytes (3 for a register, up to 50 for // the data). `rx` is nullptr for writes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the power-up and reset times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method and the optional hooks. A port with GpioSet() for CONVST and RESET and GpioGet() for DRDY lets MeasureOnce() run a whole conversion. 4. Read a frame ¶ main.cpp #include "ads9324.hpp" // This minimal port has no CONVST pin hook, so the example drives CONVST itself // (see "Drive CONVST yourself" on the API guide); ReadFrame() reads the latest // conversion. int read_ain1_microvolts ( MyPort & port , int32_t & microvolts ) { ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = adc . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. bus up, reset, DEVICE_ID, Config{} return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus, Timeout or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring } // ... pulse CONVST here, wait 1.25 us ... const auto frame = adc . ReadFrame (); // 2. one frame: all 16 channels, 16 bits each if ( ! frame ) { return static_cast < int > ( frame . error ); // DataMismatch: SDOUT stuck low or high } microvolts = frame . value . microvolts [ 0 ]; // 3. AIN1, +-5 V range, in microvolts return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , waits the power-up time, resets the chip, checks that DEVICE_ID reads 0x0004 , waits for the calibration to idle and writes Config{} : 16 channels, 16-bit words, one lane on SDOUT, ±5 V differential inputs. ReadFrame() clocks one data frame of zeros and decodes it; with a port that has GpioSet() , MeasureOnce() pulses CONVST and waits for the result first. microvolts[0] is AIN1 in microvolts, from the code and the channel's range. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() : the bus did not come up EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch The SPI mode, the wiring and IOVDD ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns Timeout The supplies and the reference: calibration stayed busy ReadFrame() returns DataMismatch SDOUT is stuck low or high ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : measurements, ranges, windows, calibration, errors. docs.text: MCU ADS9324 Notes SPI SCLK SCLK Mode 0, up to 60 MHz; 1 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI SDI SPI MISO SDOUT The registers and, in the default configuration, the data of all 16 channels GPIO (chip select) CS Low for the whole frame: one transfer per frame GPIO CONVST Idles high; the falling edge samples all 16 channels. A timer may drive it instead GPIO RESET Idles high; optional, tie it high if the port has no hook GPIO input DRDY/ALARM Optional: with it the driver waits for the result, without it for the conversion time 5 V, 1.8 V, 1.7 V to 3.6 V AVDD_5V, AVDD_1V8, IOVDD 1 µF and 0.1 µF at each supply pin GND GND, REFM, exposed pad REFSEL high selects the internal reference (the default). The Hardware page has the full pin list, the reference and the timing. Every analog input needs a series resistor: the datasheet rating is ±18 V.

docs.text: Add the repository as a submodule and link the ads9324::ads9324 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads9324.git external/driver-ads9324
docs.title: 2. Add the driver

docs.text: The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves frames. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One frame, CS held low for all `len` bytes (3 for a register, up to 50 for // the data). `rx` is nullptr for writes. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the power-up and reset times depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method and the optional hooks. A port with GpioSet() for CONVST and RESET and GpioGet() for DRDY lets MeasureOnce() run a whole conversion.
docs.title: 3. Write the port

docs.text: main.cpp #include "ads9324.hpp" // This minimal port has no CONVST pin hook, so the example drives CONVST itself // (see "Drive CONVST yourself" on the API guide); ReadFrame() reads the latest // conversion. int read_ain1_microvolts ( MyPort & port , int32_t & microvolts ) { ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MyPort > adc ( port ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = adc . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. bus up, reset, DEVICE_ID, Config{} return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus, Timeout or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring } // ... pulse CONVST here, wait 1.25 us ... const auto frame = adc . ReadFrame (); // 2. one frame: all 16 channels, 16 bits each if ( ! frame ) { return static_cast < int > ( frame . error ); // DataMismatch: SDOUT stuck low or high } microvolts = frame . value . microvolts [ 0 ]; // 3. AIN1, +-5 V range, in microvolts return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , waits the power-up time, resets the chip, checks that DEVICE_ID reads 0x0004 , waits for the calibration to idle and writes Config{} : 16 channels, 16-bit words, one lane on SDOUT, ±5 V differential inputs. ReadFrame() clocks one data frame of zeros and decodes it; with a port that has GpioSet() , MeasureOnce() pulses CONVST and waits for the result first. microvolts[0] is AIN1 in microvolts, from the code and the channel's range. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Coverage matrix ¶ docs/coverage-matrix.md has one row for each parameter of the datasheet. tools/check_matrix.py runs in tools/preflight.sh and fails when a row cites a symbol that is not in the code, a test id that is not in tests/ , or when the row counts in the header are wrong. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the ADS9324 written from the datasheet: the three register banks with the AIN9 to AIN16 bank in reverse order, the 24-bit frames and the two-frame read, the data frame in 8, 4, 2 and 1 lanes with 16- and 24-bit words, the DIAG byte and the randomizer, all 15 channel modes, the test patterns, the window comparator with its latched flags and the alarm pin, the ADC calibration with its timing, standby and the reset flag. Faults can be injected into every transfer. The tests build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_startup.cpp Lifecycle, the start-up sequence and its order, identity checks, reset, a failure injected at every transfer, standby and wake tests/test_readout.cpp Data frames: every range, clipping, offset binary, the randomizer, DIAG and PRBS, 24-bit words, all 15 channel modes, every lane count, stuck and floating lines, test patterns, the self-test tests/test_config.cpp Setters: the mirrored bank mapping of every channel, the shadow equals the chip after every setter, minimal traffic, write ordering, Verify::ReadBack , validation tests/test_features.cpp The filters and the SYSREF pulse, the window comparator and the alarm pin, the ADC calibration, the reference, the model's knobs tests/test_types.cpp Enumerations, Validate() , the pure helpers (ranges, rates, decoding) tests/test_registers.cpp The driver's register map against the model's: 116 registers, reset values, banks tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value (16 and up) is returned by some call, and the three the chip cannot produce never are tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( ads9324_fuzz_ads9324_corpus ), see below tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a void GpioSet() or GpioGet() , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a narrowed CaptureLanes() , a Log() returning int , a hook without noexcept , an invalid CheckedConfig , a daisy chain in a CheckedConfig , a class that is not a port tests/mock_ads9324.hpp The chip model, with its own register map and a Knobs struct for every assumption in Limitations tests/check_version_copy.cmake _config/Doxyfile carries the CMake version examples/host/ The host example, built with the test flags and run ( ads9324_host_example ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(ads9324) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model stands alone ¶ tests/mock_ads9324.hpp is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include ads9324_registers.hpp or ads9324_types.hpp . Its register map, field masks, reset values, timing and data-frame layout are its own, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model (handbook KB-TST-030). test_registers.cpp compares the two for every documented register, so a wrong address, reset value or bank fails a test that names the register. When that test stops, one of the two maps is wrong: check it against the datasheet section the model names, and fix that one. A new register goes into both. Every behaviour found on hardware becomes a knob or a fault mode of the model and a test that fails on the code before the fix. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_ads9324.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration, then up to 64 driver calls, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits of the data read or replace it. Between calls it can change the chip: a stuck or floating data line, a brown-out, a reset flagged in the DIAG byte, a slow calibration, the other readings of the datasheet's open questions. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines and a zero value; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer; only documented registers are written, only with documented codes (a bank, a range, a lane count, an alarm function), and no read-only register and no daisy-chain register; every readout frame sends zeros and has the length the configuration implies; the ADC calibration is never started with a digital filter on, and a configuration change never turns it off; a reset flag in a data frame leaves the driver uninitialised; every call ends: the time the port is asked to wait is bounded; while no fault is injected the shadow equals the chip after every setter; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DADS9324_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_ads9324 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_ads9324 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ads9324 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_ads9324 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ads9324/ on GCC and Clang ( ads9324_fuzz_ads9324_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( ads9324_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/ads9324.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target ads9324_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ The ESP32 example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it logs four channels twice a second. Follow the bench steps on the Limitations page, apply a known voltage to AIN9 and AIN16, and record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_ads9324.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration, then up to 64 driver calls, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits of the data read or replace it. Between calls it can change the chip: a stuck or floating data line, a brown-out, a reset flagged in the DIAG byte, a slow calibration, the other readings of the datasheet's open questions. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines and a zero value; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer; only documented registers are written, only with documented codes (a bank, a range, a lane count, an alarm function), and no read-only register and no daisy-chain register; every readout frame sends zeros and has the length the configuration implies; the ADC calibration is never started with a digital filter on, and a configuration change never turns it off; a reset flag in a data frame leaves the driver uninitialised; every call ends: the time the port is asked to wait is bounded; while no fault is injected the shadow equals the chip after every setter; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DADS9324_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_ads9324 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_ads9324 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ads9324 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_ads9324 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ads9324/ on GCC and Clang ( ads9324_fuzz_ads9324_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ).
docs.title: Fuzz tests

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DADS9324_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( ads9324_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/ads9324.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SBASB22 -: Reset: 7.4.1 Reset, p. 49 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: either EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus pins in your port against the board. With a logic analyser, check that the first frame (a write to GEN_CFG1, the software reset) appears on the bus as three bytes with CS low for all of them. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ DEVICE_ID did not read 0x0004 , or BANK_SEL did not read as the driver left it. The chip answered with something else, or nothing answered. Read value Likely cause Fix 0x0000 SDOUT not connected, or CS not reaching the chip Check SDOUT and CS continuity 0xFFFF SDOUT floating high, or the chip unpowered Check the three supplies and that SDOUT is not pulled up hard Anything else Wrong SPI mode, or a shifted bit Use mode 0; check that CS stays low for the whole 24-bit frame and that the clock is at most 29 MHz ( kMaxSdoutClockHz ; 60 MHz is the table limit for writes only) EnsureInitialized returns Timeout ¶ CALIB_BUSY did not clear after the reset. Check the three supplies, that RESET is high (or released by your GpioSet() with GpioSignal::INACTIVE ), and the reference: with ReferenceSource::External the chip needs a 4.096 V source on REFIO. EnsureInitialized returns Unsupported ¶ Config::hardware_reset is set but the port has no GpioSet() , or the configuration asks for the daisy chain (out of scope: Limitations ). EnsureInitialized returns InvalidArgument ¶ Validate() rejected the configuration and nothing was sent. Call ads9324::Validate(config) on the host to see which rule: the combinations are listed on Configuration . ReadFrame returns DataMismatch ¶ The frame is all zeros or all ones, which is what a stuck or floating SDOUT reads. A real conversion of an input at a code limit is never all 0x00 or all 0xFF across 16 channels. Check SDOUT, CS and the SPI mode. Check that a conversion happened: pulse CONVST (or use MeasureOnce() ) before ReadFrame() . Run RunDataPathSelfTest() : it uses test patterns, so it works with the inputs unconnected. When you are sure the frame is a real one, Sampling::reject_stuck_frames = false turns the check off. A channel reads another channel's value ¶ The AIN9 to AIN16 registers are in reverse order; the driver maps them, so a swap points at the wiring or at the frame layout. Check the channel count and group ( ChannelSelect ): with 8 channels the frame carries AIN1 to AIN8 or AIN9 to AIN16 only, and Frame::present_mask says which. RunDataPathSelfTest() returns DataMismatch when a channel returns another channel's pattern. Reads return UnexpectedReset ¶ The DIAG byte or RESET_DETECT_FLAG reported a reset: the chip reset since the driver started it, usually a brown-out on one of the supplies. The driver is uninitialised again; EnsureInitialized() writes the configuration again. If it repeats, check the supplies and their decoupling. Wake() returns it too when the registers did not survive standby. A reading sits at a code limit ¶ Frame::clipped_mask has the channel's bit set: the input is outside the range. Choose a larger InputRange , or check the input for a missing divider. An open input pair reads near zero code only in the open-wire safe type. The voltage is wrong by a fixed factor ¶ microvolts is computed from the channel's configured range; if you changed a channel's range outside the driver, the arithmetic uses the old one. Use SetInput() , and GetConfig().inputs[n] to see what the driver holds. Offset and gain errors of the board go into Input::offset_quarter_lsb and Input::gain . The window alert never fires, or fires at once ¶ The thresholds compare the top byte of the code (two's complement), not volts: ±40 on the top byte is ±40 x 256 codes. The flags are latched: ReadWindowFlags() shows what happened since the last ClearWindowFlags() . A window cannot be used with offset binary data ( Validate() refuses it). RunAdcCalibration returns Refused or Timeout ¶ Refused : a digital filter is on (switch it off with SetFilter() first) or the chip is in standby. Timeout : CALIB_BUSY stayed set for 150 ms; check the supplies, the reference and, for the free-running mode, that CONVST really runs. MeasureOnce returns Timeout ¶ With ReadySource::Pin the DRDY pin did not assert within Sampling::ready_timeout_us : check that Alarm::function is Drdy , the polarity and the wiring, and that CONVST really pulses. Check that your port's DelayUs() really waits: a delay that returns at once makes every timeout far too short.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Inside the ADS9324 ¶ Inside the ADS9324 Figure description and sources The ADS9324's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml inc/ads9324.hpp inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp ADS9324: Typical application ¶ ADS9324: Typical application Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side at the stated pitch; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/ads9324.hpp ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp . Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Hardware description: docs/hardware.yml Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml inc/ads9324.hpp inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp The layers, one of them yours ¶ The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.
